name: Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone Ltd
title: Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone Ltd - 532921 - Transcript Of Analysts/Investors Call Pertaining To Agreement To Acquire 100% Stake In Evos B.V.

read.thesis: Acquisition of Evos (EV ₹-equivalent €2.56bn, 11.7x CY25 EV/EBITDA, 56% margin) is a debt-funded, no-capex value play; leverage rises to 2.76x before guided return to 2.5x by FY27-end.

triggers.label: No new capex planned at Evos
triggers.quote: we do not expect any capex to increase the capacity in very near future.

summary.headline: APSEZ agrees to buy 100% of Evos BV from Igneo for EV €2.56bn (equity €1.18bn, 11.7x CY25 EV/EBITDA), all-debt funded.
summary.overview: APSEZ announced the acquisition of 100% of Evos BV from Igneo Infrastructure Partners, at an enterprise value of €2.56bn and equity value of €1.18bn, implying 11.7x CY25 EV/EBITDA. Evos reported CY25 revenue of €392m and a 56% EBITDA margin, operating eight port-based liquid terminals (6.3 million cubic metres) across five European countries. The deal is all-cash and debt funded, taking pro-forma net debt/EBITDA to 2.76x, which management expects to bring back to 2.5x by end FY27. Regulatory approvals and works council consultation start immediately; the call focused on volumes, ROCE, PAT, leverage and the management's view of the deal as a strategic (not financial) acquirer.

financial_highlights.change: Management expects this to fall materially over 2-5 years with business plan
Target double-digit within Ambition 2031; mgmt says 2-3 years

financial_highlights.metric: Cost of debt on Evos assets

financial_highlights.value: Double-digit % of revenue (as currently run by financial owner); not quantified in INR

segments.name: Evos liquid storage (Europe)
segments.commentary: Second-largest independent liquid storage operator in Europe; eight port terminals in Netherlands, Germany, Spain, Belgium and Malta, 6.3 million cubic metres capacity, 452 tanks and 63 vessel/barge berths. Handles about 37 million metric tonnes in CY25 per management, combined with APSEZ's existing ~5.5 million cubic metres in Mundra and Hazira.

segments.name: APSEZ existing liquids (Mundra, Hazira)
segments.commentary: Management says Evos will more than double APSEZ's liquid contribution versus Mundra and Hazira, taking combined capacity to roughly 11.5 million cubic metres.

guidance_outlook: Net debt/EBITDA to be 2.76x pro forma, reverting to 2.5x by end FY27; management says it aims to float around 2.5x in mid to long term.
No new capex planned at Evos near term; growth expected from price realisation, exports (diesel, other liquids) and transition to higher-value liquids (methanol, bio-methanol, SAF).
Evos expected to be EPS-accretive or dilutive? Not answered; management to follow up. Expects Evos to contribute to top line and bottom line without diluting APSEZ's EBITDA profile.
Ambition 2031 target of double-digit ROCE for Evos; management says 2-3 years, not more.
Business plan (five-year) to be shared after closing; no detailed financial forecast given on the call.
capex_capacity: Evos: 6.3 million cubic metres across eight terminals; APSEZ existing Mundra and Hazira approx. 5.5 million cubic metres; combined about 11.5 million cubic metres.
Management says land is available at Evos terminals for expansion, but expansion is not being evaluated now; priority is utilisation and value-added conversion of existing tankage.
Land tenure: mostly leasehold from port authorities (e.g. Amsterdam, Rotterdam), some leases running to 2092; one terminal freehold; leases renewed every 25-30 years at revised rates.
Key growth levers are tank turnaround ratio, operational efficiency and product mix shift rather than new tank capacity.
demand_pricing: Contracts are significantly take-or-pay and CPI-linked, with mid to long-term tier-1 blue-chip customers; value-added services include blending and pipeline connectivity to airports.
Europe mix cited as ~80% conventional and ~20% sustainable fuels today, moving toward ~50:50 in 15-20 years; management says diesel may fall 36% while biodiesel and exports rise more than 36%.
Export demand from Africa for conventional fuels already started, given refinery shortfalls.
Competitors named: Vopak and VTTI; Evos' ARA location and contract profile are cited as differentiators.
Bidding was a structured sell-side process; number of bidders not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the tonnage, and are contracts take-or-pay?
qa_highlights.answer: About 37 million metric tonnes in CY25 (from 6.3m cubic metres plus APSEZ's ~5.5m). Significant share of contracts are take-or-pay and CPI-linked, with mid to long-term customers.

qa_highlights.question: Is the deal debt-funded and what is the cost of debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Fully debt-funded. Asset cost of debt ~4.5%, versus APSEZ average funding cost of 6.4-6.6% including foreign-currency funding. Restructuring of the balance sheet is planned later.

qa_highlights.question: Why is a financial investor selling, and will this be storage-led?
qa_highlights.answer: Igneo is a financial investor with a different return horizon; APSEZ positions itself as a strategic investor. Revenue baseline is storage plus value-added services; distribution and handling are not yet confirmed.

qa_highlights.question: What is PAT, and is the deal EPS-accretive in CY27?
qa_highlights.answer: PAT not quantified. Current PAT is double-digit as % of revenue under the financial owner's structure; management expects it to converge toward APSEZ's average after reinvestment and balance sheet changes. EPS accretion question deferred to follow-up.

qa_highlights.question: What are current ROCE and valuation basis?
qa_highlights.answer: Current ROCE about 7%. The 11.7x multiple is expected to fall with the business plan; valuation method not disclosed. Payback period not provided.

qa_highlights.question: Does APSEZ plan further acquisitions and leverage limits?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says it is not chasing deals but is evaluating around 20 assets globally; it targets ~2.5x leverage on average to deliver 18-19% CAGR and says it has appetite for more acquisitions while staying selective.

risks_watch: Leverage rises to 2.76x pro forma before target 2.5x by end FY27; watch debt paydown and any FY27 guidance update.
PAT and EPS impact unquantified; follow-up promised. Payback period and business plan not yet disclosed.
Realisation of ROCE from ~7% to double digits within 2-3 years depends on product-mix shift and export flows, not capex.
Regulatory approvals and works council consultation pending in multiple European jurisdictions.
Integration of a foreign leadership team and engineering talent; management said leadership continuity is committed.
Euro-denominated earnings and debt: currency exposure and foreign-currency funding mix to be detailed offline.
summary.management_tone: Confident and strategic on the asset and long-term value creation, but evasive on specifics: PAT, EPS accretion, payback, valuation basis and the business plan were deferred to follow-up, citing the deal having just closed.
key_quotes: Evos is an extremely strategic asset for APSEZ.

This is an all -cash transaction that will be funded via debt, and on a pro -forma basis, we expect APSEZ's net debt to EBITDA to be at 2. 76x but revert to our guidance of 2.5x net debt to EBITDA by the end of FY27.
we are not after the deals, but we want deals to be after us.

growth.why: Management guides Evos ROCE from ~7% to double digits within Ambition 2031 (2-3 years) and leverage back to 2.5x by end FY27, backed by take-or-pay CPI-linked contracts, tank turnaround and product-mix shift; no new capacity or revenue growth number was given, and no new capex is planned near term.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Evos ROCE of ~7% is targeted to reach double digits within 2-3 years (Ambition 2031) via tank turnaround, product-mix shift and pricing, but no quantified EBITDA margin path was given beyond Evos' 56% CY25 margin.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Evos runs 6.3m cubic metres across eight terminals and combined APSEZ liquids reach ~11.5m cubic metres, but management says expansion is not being evaluated now and no new capacity is planned near term.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Evos handled ~37 million metric tonnes in CY25 on take-or-pay, CPI-linked contracts, and African export demand has already started, but no volume growth percentage was guided.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management says no new capex is planned at Evos near term and priority is utilisation of existing tankage, with no utilisation level disclosed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No revenue or margin guidance raise was given; the EPS accretion question was deferred and PAT was not quantified.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Pro-forma net debt/EBITDA rises to 2.76x versus the 2.5x target by end FY27, and PAT/EPS impact and payback remain unquantified.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management cites a shift to methanol, bio-methanol and SAF at Evos, but no launch dates or volumes were given.

rows.label: Export demand from Africa for conventional fuels
rows.why: African export demand has already started given refinery shortfalls, and diesel/other-liquid exports are a cited growth lever at Evos.

rows.label: Net debt/EBITDA back to 2.5x by end FY27
rows.why: Management guided pro-forma leverage of 2.76x reverting to 2.5x by end FY27, but no paydown schedule was disclosed.

rows.label: Further acquisitions from ~20 evaluated assets
rows.why: Management is evaluating around 20 assets globally and has appetite for more deals while targeting ~2.5x leverage, though it says it is not chasing deals.

tone.note: Management was confident on the strategic logic, ROCE uplift to double digits within 2-3 years and deleveraging to 2.5x by end FY27, but deferred PAT, EPS accretion, payback and valuation basis to follow-up; analysts pushed on EPS impact and leverage.
